approach.heading: How I actually approach SEO
paragraphs: Most SEO pitches are vague on purpose, "we'll boost your rankings" sounds good and commits to nothing. Here's specifically what happens.

Every page is built around how your customers actually search, not a list of keywords. That means real topic mapping tied to your specific services, not generic content stuffed with search terms. In the first 6-8 weeks I typically establish 8-10 priority topic areas across your core pages. After that, ongoing content builds on what's actually generating inquiries.

I don't guarantee rankings. Nobody honestly can, in Google or in AI search results like ChatGPT and AI Overviews. What I do guarantee is that the content is built to be genuinely useful, which is what both search engines and AI systems actually reward.

Expect page indexing and name-plus-service visibility by 3 months, traffic on more specific search terms by 6 months, and real visibility in your service area by 12 months. These are typical patterns, not promises, every industry and market moves differently.

Backlink outreach is included in the $2,000/month plan. It's organic, meaning I manually reach out to real site owners and earn genuine editorial links. Google's guidelines prohibit buying backlinks, so this is the version that actually holds up instead of putting your site at risk.

specialty.heading: SEO for Denver contractors and home service businesses.
specialty.body: Contractor and home services SEO rewards businesses that show up for the exact jobs people search for: roofing, plumbing, HVAC, remodeling, general construction. If you run a home services or contracting business in Denver, this is where I spend a lot of my time, service-area pages, project galleries that actually rank, and a Google Business Profile built around how homeowners search when something breaks.

items.question: What makes you different from other Denver SEO companies?
items.answer: Most Denver SEO companies and agencies hand you off to an account manager who relays your questions to whoever's actually doing the work that week. I am the person doing the work: audits, strategy, writing, technical fixes, all of it. You're not paying for layers of agency overhead, and you're not one account among hundreds.

items.question: How is local SEO different from regular SEO?
items.answer: Local SEO focuses on ranking for searches with local intent: 'near me' searches, the Google Map Pack, and location-based keywords. It relies heavily on your Google Business Profile, citations, and location-specific content, on top of standard technical and on-page SEO.

items.question: Do you guarantee first-page rankings?
items.answer: No, and anyone who guarantees specific rankings is being dishonest with you. Google's algorithm isn't something any agency controls. What I can guarantee is a thorough, technically sound strategy and transparent reporting on real progress.

items.question: How much does SEO cost per month?
items.answer: It depends on your market and how competitive your keywords are. See the Pricing page for typical ranges, or book a call and I'll give you a straight answer based on your situation.

items.question: Can you do SEO on my current website?
items.answer: In most cases, yes. I'll audit your current site first and let you know if there are technical limitations worth addressing before we start.

items.question: Will this get me ranked in AI search results (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, etc.)?
items.answer:
I can't guarantee specific rankings, in AI search or regular Google results. Anyone who guarantees that isn't being straight with you. What I can tell you is that I write content worth reading, so both search engines and AI systems recognize it as genuinely useful.

AI systems like Google's AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Bing pull from content that demonstrates real expertise, not keyword-stuffed pages. That means structuring your site around what you actually do, using clear signals (who you are, what you're qualified to do, the specific problems you solve), and building authority through real proof, not tricks.

On the technical side, I implement schema markup so search engines and AI systems understand who you are and what your business does. There's no such thing as a "ChatGPT optimization trick." I build visibility through content that's actually worth citing.

items.question: How many pages will my website have?
items.answer:
It depends on how many distinct services you offer, not a fixed number. If your business does three genuinely different things, the people searching for each of those want different answers, so each gets its own page instead of one page trying to cover everything.

A typical build includes a home page, an about page, a services overview, individual pages for each core service, and a contact page. The structure is built to grow. As we learn what your customers actually search for, we add pages. I don't pad a site with pages nobody needs just to hit a number.

items.question: What SEO strategy do you actually use?
items.answer:
People-first SEO. I map your content to how your customers actually search, not to a list of individual keywords. Nobody searches a single word like "plumber." They search phrases tied to a real problem they're trying to solve.

Each core page targets a few priority topics that match what your customers are actually trying to figure out when they land on that page. If you've got your own research, a list from an industry group, or ideas from your own experience with customers, send it over. That's valuable data and I'll build it into the site structure. I won't stuff those terms into the copy, I'll build genuine content around what they actually mean, because that's what ranks long-term and what turns a visitor into a customer.

items.question: How do you decide which search terms to go after, and how many can you realistically cover?
items.answer:
Priority comes down to three things: your core services, how your customers actually search, and content depth, meaning quality over quantity.

In the first 6-8 weeks, I typically target 8-10 primary topic areas across your core pages. That's not an attempt to rank for 50 keywords at once. It's about establishing real authority in what you actually do.

After launch, ongoing content extends that coverage based on the inquiries you're actually getting and what's changing in your industry.

Rough timeline: by 3 months, your core pages should be indexed and ranking for your business name plus your core service terms. By 6 months, you should start seeing traffic for more specific searches. By 12 months, you should have real visibility for the broader searches in your service area. These are general patterns, not guarantees. Results vary by industry and competition.

items.question: Is SEO part of the website build, or does it start separately?
items.answer:
SEO isn't a phase I bolt on after the site is built, it's baked into the build itself. Site speed, mobile optimization, clean code, URL structure, heading hierarchy, internal linking, and basic schema markup are all part of the build, not an add-on.

In the first 6-8 weeks: technical SEO foundation, core page content, internal linking, and structured data so search engines understand who you are.

After launch: ongoing content strategy, backlink outreach, and quarterly reviews of every page's performance. We'll have monthly calls to go over what's working, and I'll reach out directly if something needs your input in between.

items.question: Who writes the content, and who's responsible for what?
items.answer: I write all the initial content. You review it for accuracy and make sure it sounds like you. I handle all the technical implementation. After launch, we set a cadence for new content together and decide when to expand into new topics based on what's actually generating inquiries.

items.question: Do you build backlinks? How?
items.answer:
Yes, backlink outreach is included in the $2,000/month SEO plan. It's organic outreach, meaning I manually reach out to real website owners and earn genuine, editorial links, not purchased ones.

Google's own guidelines prohibit buying backlinks. Any agency selling you a package of links at a flat rate, especially the ones that lead with inflated metrics like "DA 90+," is selling you something that can get your site penalized, not something that helps it. Real outreach is slower, but it's the version that doesn't put your site at risk.
